findings.explanation: `done` initially receives the fourth argument, `name` the second, and `opts` the truthy third argument or `null`. A callable second argument replaces `done` and clears both the alternate name and options. Otherwise, a callable third argument replaces `done`, preserves the alternate name, and clears `opts`. The following independent branch promotes the second argument to options exactly when `typeof filename === 'object'` and the third argument is either callable or `undefined`; it clears `name` and restores that object as `opts` without changing `done`. Consequently, a third-position callback normalized by the preceding branch is retained, and when the third position is undefined the initially captured fourth callback is retained. After attachment and path derivation, download dynamically calls `this.sendFile(fullPath, opts, done)`—normally the capital-F public method—with the computed path, derived options, and normalized callback. It does not initiate a second transfer or call the lowercase private helper directly.

The attachment name is `basename(name || path)`: a truthy alternate name is used, while no name or an empty-string name falls back to the original source path. This affects only Content-Disposition; `fullPath` is always derived from `path`, never from `name`. A fresh headers object starts with the generated Content-Disposition. `Object.keys(opts.headers)` copies only the user's own enumerable headers, and lowercasing each key prevents any casing of `Content-Disposition` from replacing the generated value. The derived options object is `Object.create(opts)`, so a supplied plain options object is its prototype and non-header options are inherited rather than copied. With no options, `opts` is `null`, producing a null-prototype derived object. The fresh headers object is installed as an own property, shadowing any inherited `headers`. In this repository code, the original options and original headers objects are not assigned to; the public sendFile method's later `etag` assignment lands on the derived object under the stated ordinary-data-property assumptions. Imported-module behavior is outside scope. At resolution time, a truthy inherited or own `root` preserves the original `path`; a missing or falsey `root` invokes `resolve(path)`. This handoff itself establishes no filesystem-containment guarantee.

The capital-F `res.sendFile` is the public entry point. Its lowercase `sendfile` target is a lexical private function at line 921; there is no lowercase response method in this repository. `done` starts as the third argument and `opts` is the supplied truthy options object or a fresh object. A callable second argument is normalized to `done` with another fresh options object. Validation precedes transfer setup: omitted, null, empty-string, and other falsey paths take the required-path error; a truthy non-string takes the type error; and a path for which `pathIsAbsolute` is false is rejected unless `opts.root` is truthy. It then computes `pathname` with `encodeURI`, overwrites/creates `opts.etag` from the application setting, and passes the same request, pathname, and options to imported `send`. The resulting `file`, same `opts`, and response are handed to private `sendfile`, whose terminal callback enters the shown closure. There is no `try`/`catch`: validation errors and any synchronous failure before that call propagate and never reach the private helper or completion callback. A synchronous throw during the private helper's own listener/pipe setup occurs after entry but likewise is not converted to completion.

Every private-helper terminal result returns through this closure: success supplies `undefined`, while terminal failures supply an error. If the normalized user callback exists—including one propagated from download—it receives that value and the immediate return disables all automatic routing. Without a callback, `EISDIR` is routed first as bare `next()`. Any other error is routed as `next(err)` only if its code is not `ECONNABORTED` and its syscall is not `write`; abort errors and write errors are left unrouted here. Successful completion without a callback also performs no `next` call. This code does not generate statuses or make decisions about whether response bytes have already been sent.

Before piping, private `sendfile` registers five file listeners in this order: `directory` terminates with a newly created `EISDIR` error; `end` terminates successfully; `error` terminates with the original error; `file` only sets `streaming = false`; and `stream` only sets `streaming = true`. It then registers response completion through `onFinished(res, onfinish)`, conditionally registers `headers`, and finally calls `file.pipe(res)`. This registration order does not assert an emission or network-timing order. Terminal handlers share a per-transfer `done` flag, check it, and set it before invoking the callback, suppressing repeated or callback-reentrant terminal notifications. Header application is not performed during setup: a listener is installed only if `options.headers` is truthy then. If installed, the event handler re-reads `options.headers` at event time, snapshots its own enumerable keys with `Object.keys`, and forwards each current value to the response argument's `setHeader`. Thus adding headers after an initially falsey value installs no listener, while replacing or mutating an initially present plain headers object before the event is observable. A terminal path reached without a `headers` emission performs no header loop; once headers have been applied, later failure handlers contain no rollback. The headers listener also has no `done` guard. No behavior of the imported file emitter or `on-finished` is inferred.

`streaming` begins undefined. A `stream` event changes it to true and a `file` event changes it to false; the deferred closure reads the variable when it executes, so the latest observed state—not a snapshot taken by `onfinish`—controls its branch. A finish error with code `ECONNRESET` is immediately translated through guarded `onaborted` into a new `Request aborted` error with code `ECONNABORTED`; another finish error goes immediately through guarded `onerror` unchanged. A no-error finish returns if already done, otherwise schedules `setImmediate`. When that callback runs, undefined or true `streaming` while not done is classified as an abort. Exactly false `streaming` while not done completes successfully. If `end`, `directory`, `error`, an abort, or another deferred finish completes in the interim, the shared `done` checks suppress the pending or repeated callback. Multiple no-error finish notifications could schedule multiple deferred functions before completion, but only the first still eligible to terminate can call back. These are source-level state transitions only; they imply no particular external event or network ordering.
